critique.evidence: Strong, cohesive defense-console aesthetic: disciplined near-black palette, restrained cyan/green/amber accents, bold headline, and consistent technical typography. However, desktop composition is unbalanced by a large empty upper-right area and an oversized decorative left panel, while the results content feels compressed. Mobile becomes very dense: tiny metadata/table text, awkward headline wrapping, a two-line overlay button, and long evidence strings weaken legibility and polish. Tablet is the strongest layout. The global header is crisp on desktop, but tablet/mobile navigation is visibly clipped with only a subtle “MORE” cue.
critique.fix: Rebalance desktop by widening or elevating the results panel and reducing the decorative panel’s dominance. On mobile, increase supporting-text sizes, shorten/wrap hashes deliberately, simplify the evidence table, and keep the regression button to one line. Give the horizontally clipped header navigation a clearer overflow affordance and verify contrast for muted labels.
